prize_parts.citation: For developing targeted protein degradation, using small molecules to direct the ubiquitin-proteasome system to destroy chosen proteins

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation turns a biological process, ubiquitin-dependent proteolysis, into something chemists can design. A heterobifunctional PROTAC or a monovalent molecular glue induces a ternary complex that does not exist in nature, so a protein is removed rather than merely inhibited. The principle is original, mechanistically clean and general across target classes. It has also changed practice: proteins once called undruggable are now approached with small molecules, and degraders are in advanced clinical trials. It is the only shortlisted candidate that both founded a design principle and spread across chemical biology, medicinal chemistry and clinical development. Seven of eight members ranked it, and Chabes and I put it first, which is a broader base than any other candidate has.
statement.case_against: Credit is fragmented. PROTAC and molecular-glue work arguably form two lineages, with Crews and Deshaies on one side and Handa and Ito on the other, and Ciulli, Sakamoto, Gray and Kim all have real claims. A three-person prize cannot honour them all. Clinical validation is also incomplete, because no PROTAC drug has been approved. Committee support is broad but shallow: five of seven rankings are 3rd, 4th or 8th, so it may not survive a majority vote against a candidate with intense backing.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks B068 third and values it as a new therapeutic modality, but credits Ciulli rather than Handa as the third laureate because of the VHL ligand and structure-guided design.
responses.response: I take the Ciulli case seriously. His VHL ligand work and ternary-complex structures made PROTACs chemically rational and drug-like. But the cereblon discovery by Handa and Ito explains thalidomide and its analogues, which are the molecular glues that reached patients first, so Handa anchors the second major branch. I prefer the three names that span both branches, and I would not oppose Ciulli replacing Handa if the committee decides that PROTACs are the core. I do not think the decision should be fixed before we have discussed it.

responses.point: Somfai ranks Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling first as the clearest case of a general method, simple in concept, used daily in synthesis and with a clean two-person credit, and ranks PROTACs only eighth.
responses.response: I agree with the attribution and the breadth of use. My reservation is novelty. Buchwald-Hartwig amination is a major extension of the 2010 cross-coupling prize, and Chabes makes the same point. Impact in practice is not the same as a new concept. PROTACs do more than deliver a method: they define a new mode of pharmacology, and chemists are still finding what that opens up. I would also ask Somfai whether the 2010 precedent weighs against B011. If it does not, I consider it the strongest alternative to B068.

responses.point: Brzezinski ranks B068 eighth, saying the field has many valid claimants, and puts long-range protein electron transfer (Gray and Winkler) and nitrogenase first and second for their physical grounding.
responses.response: The many-claimants objection is fair and I accept it as a real risk. I do not accept that it lowers the scientific rank, because crowded credit shows the field is large and independently reproduced. On B053, Gray and Winkler gave a quantitative, tested physical picture of tunnelling through proteins, but it has been reported for decades and has not obviously changed what other researchers or clinicians can do. For me the test is what has been enabled, and I would like Peter to explain what B053 has enabled beyond its explanatory value.

responses.point: Linke, the chair, ranks dye-sensitized solar cells first for their clear kinetic principle and clean two-name credit, and ranks PROTACs fourth.
responses.response: Grätzel and O'Regan have an unusually clean attribution and a quantitative principle, and the link to perovskite devices makes it a lasting field. My concern is that the committee should weigh how much a recognition changes practice. Dye-sensitized cells reached niche markets and their main legacy is conceptual. I would rank B039 above B011 on principle but below B068 on consequence, and I do not think the chair's ranking and mine are far apart.

uncertainties: Whether the committee wants the PROTAC and molecular-glue lineages in one prize or sees them as separate, which decides whether Handa or Ciulli takes the third place.
Whether the lack of an approved PROTAC drug is judged premature, and whether I am underweighting that because of my translational orientation.
Whether B063 is read as chemistry or as pharmaceutics, and whether its credit among six names can be settled.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. My Linköping affiliation and biosensor work have no direct link to the PROTAC or lipid nanoparticle candidates. I have some research overlap with Emma Sparr on self-assembly, but that does not bear on B068.
